strategy.summary: Reproduce the VIF instability from issue #9791 / PR #9835 by running the new test_vif_instability in statsmodels/stats/tests/test_influence.py, built from source. The test is deterministic (seed 42 at the top, and clean_exog draws from the same seeded stream). On the buggy revision it should fail at the first variance_inflation_factor call because the standardize keyword does not exist yet, so the failure is a TypeError rather than a numerical mismatch. On the fixed revision it should pass. The numerical claims (inf, explosion, warnings) are only checked indirectly by the test's later assertions.

strategy.success_criterion: Buggy revision 383d9707516a: the test FAILS. The first call variance_inflation_factor(exog, 0, standardize=True) raises TypeError (unexpected keyword 'standardize'), so the test never reaches the numerical assertions. Fixed revision (PR #9835 applied): the test PASSES. Its three parts pass: standardize=True gives VIF about 1.0 for the intercept with no UserWarning; standardize=False on the badly scaled data emits 'The design matrix is poorly conditioned' and returns a value > 100; and on clean_exog, standardize=True and standardize=False agree to rtol=1e-7.
strategy.numerical_probe: On the buggy revision, call variance_inflation_factor(exog, 1, standardize=False) on the badly scaled exog from the test and observe whether it warns and returns an unstable value. Use that only to confirm the numerical behaviour once the keyword exists; the transition itself is decided by the test.
risks: The buggy revision fails for an API reason (no standardize keyword) before any numerical check runs, so the failure does not isolate the numerical bug. A stronger check would call standardize=False alone on the buggy revision, but the developer's test is the graded transition.

The test is platform-sensitive: exact VIF magnitudes and whether 1 - rsquared hits floating-point zero depend on the BLAS, the CPU and the numpy build. The warning and the >100 threshold may not reproduce on other platforms, so the numerical part of the test may not transition there.

numpy version is unbounded in the evidence. numpy 2 changes floating-point and dtype behaviour and may change the magnitude or presence of the instability, so the numpy<2 pin is an inference, not a documented constraint.
Python version is not stated, so the environment may not build the Cython extensions on very new Python versions.
The test file test_outliers_influence.py was also changed to pass standardize=False. That test uses a Stata reference (16.4394) and is a separate check. It is not the reproducing test for this bug.

The test contains no explicit seed for the clean data beyond the seed set at the top of the function. The result depends on the random draw order from np.random.seed(42) and on the uniform calls preceding the normal draw, so any change to those calls changes the data.
The final signature is unclear: the review asked for keyword-only standardize, but the diff still has it positional. The test passes standardize as a keyword, so either signature works for the test.
The tolerance in the oracle (rtol=1e-7) is tight. Floating-point differences from BLAS or CPU vectorisation could make clean-data equality fail on some platforms even on the fixed revision.

oracle.tolerance: rtol=1e-7 (clean-data equality of standardize=True and standardize=False); vif_legacy > 100 threshold; atol=1e-2 for the intercept VIF near 1.0
oracle.reference_source: The test assertions in test_vif_instability itself, derived from the PR #9835 diff
oracle.why: The assertions are the developer's stated oracle and are the only graded outcome. The rtol and threshold values are taken directly from the test, not invented.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On the buggy revision, variance_inflation_factor does not accept the standardize keyword, so the first call at variance_inflation_factor(exog, 0, standardize=True) raises TypeError. The test fails there, before any numerical assertion runs.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: On the fixed revision, the standardize keyword exists. The intercept VIF is about 1.0, the badly scaled case warns with 'The design matrix is poorly conditioned' and returns a value > 100, and the clean-data standardize=True and standardize=False results agree to rtol=1e-7. The test passes.
